13.text: “Mouse-Driver” (Pɪpᴇˊkɪlhᴀ-hekeˊñɪlɪn) forms one of the favorite figures

14.text: of cat’s-cradles among Chukchee children (Fig. 202). One of the reindeer-

16.text: The conception of “owners” of places is more highly developed among

17.text: the Russianized Yukaghir of the Kolyma and Anadyr. This is probably

18.text: because the ancient native elements have been mixed with Russian mytholo-

19.text: gical ideas. According to their belief, the “masters” of the places live like

20.text: men, but are more powerful. They have houses and villages, travel about

21.text: the country with sledges, and drive foxes and wolves instead of dogs.

22.text: Every “master” of a particular forest owns all the game living in that forest;

23.text: the “master” of a river owns the fish living in it, etc.

24.text: “Masters” of the forest are, in the Russo-Yukaghir conception, exceed-
